 Judgment
This appeal is filed by the appellant/claimant in O.P (MV) No.1366 of 2007 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Kottayam.
The respondents herein are the respondents before the tribunal.

2. According to the appellant/claimant, on 10.06.2007 at about 01.45 pm, while the petitioner was riding a motorcycle with his two friends, a bus bearing registration No.KL-05-L-8969 driven by the 3rd respondent in a rash and negligent manner knocked down the motorcycle and thereby the petitioner sustained serious injuries.
The appellant approached the tribunal claiming a total compensation of 10,07,000/- limited to 5,00,000/-.
3. Respondents 1 and 3 remained ex parte before the tribunal.
The 2nd respondent insurer filed a written statement, admitting the policy, but disputing the quantum of compensation claimed.
Before the tribunal, oral testimonies of PWs 1 to 4 were adduced on the side of the petitioner.
Exts. A1
to A50 were marked.

The tribunal, after analysing the pleadings and materials on record, awarded a sum of 4,71,672/- as compensation under different MACA NO. 222 OF 2014 2025:KER:39645 heads with interest @7.5% per annum from the date of petition till realization with proportionate costs from respondent-insurer.
Dissatisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the tribunal, the claimant has come up in appeal.
4. Heard the learned counsel for the appellant and the learned Standing Counsel for the respondent insurance company.

5. The learned counsel for the appellant claims enhancement mainly under the following heads :-
Notional income :- The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that though an amount of 225/- per day was claimed as the daily income of the appellant, the tribunal has taken only an amount of 4,000/-.

The learned counsel further submitted that even going by the judgment in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236] the income of a coolie fixed for the accident which occurred in the year 2007 will come to 6,000/-.

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In order to award a just and reasonable compensation, I find that the income fixed as per the judgment in Ramachandrappa (supra) can be followed.
Accordingly, I am inclined to refix the monthly income of the appellant at 6,000/-.
Loss of earnings :- The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that towards the head loss of earnings, the tribunal has taken only a period of seven months for awarding compensation.
Considering the nature of injuries sustained, I am inclined to grant a period of eight months for awarding compensation.

Since the notional monthly income is refixed at 6,000/-,
the total compensation payable under the head is recalculated thus:
48,000/- (6,000x8).

The tribunal has already awarded an amount of 28,000/-
Binu vs Peethambaran on 5 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113809430/
2 under the said head.
Thus, there will be an additional amount of 20,000/- under the head loss of earnings.
Pain and sufferings :-
The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that though an amount of 50,000/- was claimed by the appellant, the tribunal has awarded only an amount of 30,000/-.
Considering the fact that the nature of injuries as well as age of the appellant, I find that a total amount of 50,000/- can be awarded under the head.
Thus, there will be an additional amount of 20,000/- under the afore head.
Loss of amenities :

- The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that though an amount of 2,00,000/- was claimed by the appellant, the tribunal has awarded only an amount of MACA NO. 222 OF 2014 2025:KER:39645 25,000/-.
Considering the fact that the nature of injuries as well as age of the appellant, I find that a total amount of 50,000/- can be awarded under the head.
Thus, there will be an additional amount of 25,000/- under the afore head.
Compensation for permanent disability :-
The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that while awarding compensation the tribunal has not added future prospects to the income fixed.

Considering the fact that the appellant was seriously injured and there was an amputation of the leg, I find that this is a fit case where 40%
of future prospects has to be added to the income now fixed by this Court.

By adding future prospects to the income fixed, the amount will be 8,400/- (6,000+
6,000x40%) for awarding compensation under the head loss of disability.
The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the medical board has assessed the percentage of disability at 46%.
The learned counsel further submitted that the appellant was a mason by profession and due to the amputation, he was not able to continue with the said work.
It is further submitted that since the amputation was above the knee, according to the Employees Compensation Act, 1923, the percentage of disability will come to 60%.

Considering the fact that he was a mason,
I find that the percentage of functional disability can be fixed at 60%.

Accordingly the compensation payable under the head is recalculated thus: 10,28,160/-
(8,400x12x17x60/100).

The tribunal has already awarded an amount of 3,75,360/-
under the said head.
Thus, there will be an additional amount of 6,52,800/- under the head compensation for disability.

6. Though the appellant claimed enhancement of compensation under the other heads, on a perusal of the records available, I am not inclined to interfere with the compensation awarded by the tribunal under other heads since it appears to be just and reasonable.

7. Thus, the impugned award of the tribunal is modified as follows:-

Accordingly, the appeal is allowed in part and the appellant/claimant is awarded an additional compensation of 7,17,800/- (Rupees seven lakh seventeen thousand eight hundred only) over and above the compensation awarded by the tribunal with interest @7% per annum from the date of petition till realization and proportionate costs.
The respondent insurer shall deposit the said amount together with interest and costs within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.

The claimant shall furnish copies of the PAN Card, ADHAAR Card and bank details before the respondent insurer within a period of one month so as to enable the insurance MACA NO. 222 OF 2014 2025:KER:39645 company to make the deposit as ordered above.
In case of failure to furnish details as above, it shall be open for the insurance company to deposit the said amount before the tribunal.

Upon such deposit being made, the entire amount Binu vs Peethambaran on 5 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113809430/
4 shall be disbursed to the appellant at the earliest in accordance with law.
However, it is made clear that the enhanced compensation will not carry interest for the period of delay of 325 days in filing the appeal.
